one_liner: A professional, membership-based podcast and video content studio in Tel Aviv, riding the video-podcast boom that's nearly doubled YouTube TV viewing hours in a year.
problem: Video podcasting has become a mainstream media format at remarkable speed -- YouTube users streamed over 700 million hours of video podcasts on TVs in October 2025, nearly double the 400 million hours from a year earlier, and more than 70% of podcasters now incorporate video into their shows. Producing this properly requires real equipment and space: multi-camera setups, lighting, and soundproofing that most creators, founders, and small businesses can't build themselves. In Tel Aviv specifically, the only comparable option found is a free recording studio opened in 2022 by ThoughtLeaders, an influencer-marketing company, offered as a promotional perk rather than a dedicated, reliably available paid business -- leaving working professionals and creators without a real paid studio option.
solution: Cue is a membership and hourly-rental video and podcast studio offering professional multi-camera recording setups, lighting, and light production support, positioned for founders, creators, and businesses who want to participate in the video-podcast boom without building their own studio. This is a proven, replicable business format -- multiple turn-key podcast studio rental businesses operate successfully and are actively bought and sold in US markets like Los Angeles and Nashville -- just not yet established as a dedicated paid business in Israel.
why_now: The underlying behavior is accelerating fast and globally documented: video podcast viewing hours nearly doubled year-over-year, and 53% of US podcast consumers now prefer watching over just listening. Marketplaces like PeerSpace ($40M raised, operating across major global cities) and Israel's own Splacer prove real commercial demand for bookable creative and production spaces -- but both are listings marketplaces connecting renters to existing spaces, not a dedicated, purpose-built studio brand. That leaves the owned-and-operated studio model itself as the open lane in this market.

gates.label: Product, Not Tech
gates.note: A physical studio and service business; booking software is a small supporting layer, not the product itself.

gates.label: Capital
gates.note: Single studio buildout with standard professional-grade equipment fits comfortably within a lean starting check.

gates.label: Invention
gates.note: An original, SGG-designed and owned studio brand -- not an import of an existing company's actual brand or products, so it's invention, not transfer.

gates.label: Buildable Team
gates.note: Studio operations and light production support -- standard hiring.

gates.label: Defined Claim
gates.note: Testable via one studio's booking rate and membership signups against a defined target.

gates.label: Edge
gates.note: The only Tel Aviv precedent found is a free promotional space tied to a marketing company, not a paid dedicated business; adjacent marketplaces (PeerSpace, Splacer) prove real demand for bookable creative space without themselves operating a purpose-built studio, leaving real room to differentiate as the owned-and-operated version.

business_plan.problem: Video podcasting is booming, but Tel Aviv has no dedicated, professionally-run paid studio -- only a single free promotional space tied to a marketing company.
business_plan.solution_and_model: A membership and hourly-rental video/podcast studio with professional equipment and light production support, following a proven, replicable US business format.
business_plan.market_and_edge: Video podcast viewing hours nearly doubled year-over-year globally; the only Tel Aviv precedent is free and promotional, not a real paid business; adjacent marketplaces (PeerSpace, Splacer) prove demand for bookable creative space without themselves being a dedicated studio operator.
business_plan.key_challenges: Existing space-rental marketplaces like Splacer could list competing spaces once the category proves out, and building a reliable creator community takes real marketing -- mitigated by leading with professional-grade equipment and service quality a marketplace listing can't easily replicate.
business_plan.go_to_market: Launch one flagship Tel Aviv studio targeting founders, creators, and small businesses already active in the video-podcast trend, cross-list on marketplaces like Splacer as a secondary booking channel, and prove membership retention before considering a second location.
